Multi-Site Manager - (HOP)

 

Deliveroo

Deliveroo is on a mission to be the definitive food company. We want to be the platform that people turn to whenever they think about food. We continue to operate in a competitive marketplace but have achieved so much over the past year, including significant growth in our Hop, Grocery, Editions, Signature & Plus businesses.

We continue to innovate and challenge ourselves on what we should deliver next to achieve our mission. We are investing and building out teams to help us launch new innovative products. It's an exciting time to join and while we have made great progress, we are just getting started!

Deliveroo HOP

Deliveroo HOP launched in September 2021 and is Deliveroo’s speedy grocery delivery service. Our mission is to deliver groceries to customers around the world in as little as 10 minutes - from the weekly shop, to a last minute dinner party or a late night snack. Working with trusted grocers, Deliveroo Hop promises to bring customers the very best products at lightning speed.

The team behind Deliveroo HOP are building a network of stores across London, the UK and International markets. Each delivery store is staffed with a team who have been specially trained to manage the operations efficiently as well as pick and pack orders in record time, with Deliveroo’s 100,000 strong rider network completing all deliveries.

We’re looking for people with an exceptional drive and entrepreneurial spirit to join the team at Deliveroo Hop and help us build the leading speedy grocery delivery service. Hungry to win? This is an exciting time to join the Deliveroo HOP team within the broader Deliveroo organisation - we’re only just getting started!

 

The Role

The role of the Multi-Site Manager is to drive the highest performance possible within their respective cluster of sites. This includes maximising customer satisfaction, optimising productivity and achieving site personnel costs, maintaining strong stock accuracy, tightly controlling inventory and minimising all wastage.

The Multi-Site Manager must also create a positive and cooperative working environment for all colleagues, develop and train team members to the highest standard, and ensure at all times that their operation remains safe, legal and compliant.

What You’ll be Doing

  • Plan your work week most effectively splitting time between your respective sites to ensure you are having the greatest impact possible whilst ensuring compliance to company work expectations (e.g. weekend working, late night working, time spent on site).

  • Lead through your respective teams, working closely with the Assistant Manager in your respective sites (2-4), to achieve all company objectives and goals. This will require an ability to lead effectively at a distance whilst also remaining willing and able to get stuck in!

  • Lead in accordance with the Deliveroo values and ensure your team follows suit. Act as a People Manager for all our staff colleagues and support them throughout their organisational life cycle. This includes the requirement to manage HR/ER cases.

  • Recruit and onboard HOP team members within your respective remit.

  • Develop, train and motivate all employees to achieve ambitious targets

  • Demonstrate operational excellence by meeting KPI targets across your respective sites constantly seeking to improve.

  • Minimise wastage within your respective sites by supervising regular stock counts, inventory management and supervising stock rotation.

  • Supervise compliance to company standard operating procedures (SOPs) through robust supervision, impactful coaching and inspirational leadership.

  • Drive strong standards within your sites, adhering to merchandising and space management principles in addition to delivering a clean, tidy, organised site environment.

  • Be responsible for ensuring compliance with all Health & Safety and Due Diligence measures in place for the operation. Ensure all product recalls and withdrawals are actioned as per company guidelines.

  • Complete high quality schedules for your respective sites adhering to company labour targets and working time directive requirements. Supervise accurate timekeeping and manage team holiday entitlements in the most effective way.

  • Carry out regular Health & Safety checks, including completion of requisite internal audits to monitor compliance to standards.

  • Host and participate in relevant meetings.

  • Monitor customer feedback seeking opportunities to improve the customer experience.

  • Maintain good relations to uphold Deliveroo’s positive reputation with all external parties, e.g.neighbours, landlords, contractors.

  • Liaise with your various counterparts across the business to improve overall operational performance.

  • Participate and/or lead projects, initiatives and activities to improve the operating model and achieve company objectives

Requirements

  • Minimum of 3-4 years of grocery experience

  • A good understanding and track record in managing and influencing the P&L and KPIs performance of your business

  • Capability and track record for project management

  • Possess a commercial acumen with an ability to identify opportunities to grow Order Volume & Gross Merchandise Value (GMV)

  • Great knowledge of food safety and health and safety compliance requirements

  • Previous experience in leading a team, including recruiting, training, and developing team members

  • Can demonstrate excellent communication skills, both verbally and written

  • Highly organised individual with exceptional attention to detail who has the ability to apply project management skills to tackle various challenges

  • Tech-savvy and comfortable working with numbers and using data to inform your decisions (experience with Looker preferred)

  • ‘Can do, never give up’ attitude and the desire to grow and succeed with one of the world's fastest growing food-tech companies

  • Right to work in the UK

  • Ability and willingness to travel between multiple locations on a regular basis, including overnight stays

  • Able to comply to company working expectations (e.g. weekend and late night working)

Our decisioning is built on Open Banking and cashflow underwriting rather than credit scores alone. For a higher-APR population acquired through marketplaces, seeing real affordability is what lets us select and price better than the market. The interesting product problem is that richer data comes at a cost to conversion, so the job is to capture that data advantage while designing a journey and offer that customers actually complete.

The defining challenge is balance: scaling volume by an order of magnitude while building a book of genuinely good credit quality. The best people in this space know that those two goals can be reconciled rather than traded off, and are curious enough to work out how.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the Express / Mid-prime product: proposition, roadmap, performance and economics, with direct accountability for the balance between growth and credit quality.

  • Lead how we quote and present offers across aggregator and price-comparison marketplaces, optimising eligibility, risk-based pricing and offer presentation to win the right customers at the point of acquisition.

  • Own conversion through the journey, from quote to disbursal, including how we ask customers for Open Banking data and how that affects drop-off and the quality of the book.

  • Understand and actively manage adverse selection in marketplace-acquired lending, shaping offer, pricing and decisioning strategy to attract the customers we want and screen out the risk we do not.

  • Work with data science to make sure our credit models are calibrated and tuned for this population rather than inherited unchanged from prime or adjacent segments, and be able to get into the data yourself when needed.

  • Use credit and commercial insight to optimise unit economics, balancing approval rates, pricing, loss rates and volume so the product scales profitably.

  • Monitor product and portfolio performance across the customer lifecycle, spotting emerging trends, risks and opportunities early.

  • Shape underwriting strategy, segmentation, credit policy and decisioning logic in partnership with risk and data science.

  • Design and evaluate experiments and strategy changes, and turn the analysis into clear, actionable recommendations.

  • Own the management information for the segment: define the metrics, monitoring and reporting that let the business make consistent decisions about the product.

  • Assess new initiatives, customer segments and product changes with both a commercial and a credit lens.

  • Present clear, structured updates on product performance to senior leadership and governance forums, and support funding and due diligence conversations where the product is in focus.

Who you are

  • A product person at heart: you care about the customer, the journey and the commercial outcome, and you want to own something end to end.

  • Quantitative and hands-on. You are comfortable in SQL and Python (or similar), you can interrogate a dataset yourself, and you can hold your own in a conversation with data scientists about model performance and calibration.

  • Credit-literate. You understand how eligibility, pricing and underwriting decisions shape the book you end up with, and you have a working understanding of adverse selection and why it matters in marketplace lending.

  • Commercially sharp, with a solid grasp of unit economics and a clear understanding that product decisions in lending have to work for both growth and portfolio performance.

  • Curious about trade-offs rather than defensive about them: alert to the fact that deeper affordability assessment can hurt conversion, and motivated by the challenge of capturing its value without sacrificing growth.

  • Able to move between detail and direction: happy getting into the data on a Tuesday and shaping the roadmap on a Wednesday.

  • Confident challenging assumptions and turning analysis into practical action, and able to explain your reasoning clearly to people who are not analysts.

  • Collaborative and credible with risk, commercial, engineering and data science teams.

  • Structured, proactive and comfortable in a scaling environment where priorities evolve quickly and ownership is expected.

Experience and background

  • Around four to five years of experience in product, credit strategy, analytics or a closely related role within consumer lending or fintech. We are deliberately targeting this level: this is a step-up role for someone ready to own a product, not a lateral move for someone who has run several.

  • Experience in unsecured consumer lending, ideally Unsecured Personal Loans (UPL), with exposure to the mechanics of acquiring customers through price-comparison or aggregator marketplaces. Direct experience in higher-APR or near-prime lending is a strong plus but not a prerequisite.

  • Hands-on data skills: SQL as a minimum, and ideally Python or R for analysis. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you need to be able to work alongside them as a peer and do your own analysis.

  • Experience working with or alongside credit decisioning, scorecards or risk models, and an understanding of how they are built, monitored and adjusted for a specific population.

  • Some experience of pricing, eligibility or offer design, and of using experiments or A/B tests to evaluate changes.

  • A track record of using analysis to influence decisions, not just to report on outcomes, in a role where you had some accountability for commercial results.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clearly to senior stakeholders.

  • Experience with Open Banking data or cashflow underwriting is a plus, as is experience in a fast-growing fintech.

What we offer:

  • Everyone owns a piece of the company - equity

  • Hybrid with 3 days a week in the office

  • 25 days’ holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays

  • 2 paid volunteering days per year

  • One month paid sabbatical after 4 years

  • Employee loan

  • Free gym membership

  • Team wellness budget to be active together - set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering

Join our expanding Product Growth team! We’re actively recruiting a Senior Growth Marketing Manager as we continue to scale at M-KOPA. Most senior growth hires get one channel and one pod for years. This role is built differently: you’ll own two of our core growth pods in your first year, then land where you’ve had the most impact. It’s a fast track to pod leadership, not a support seat.

The Impact 💚

You’ll drive the conversion growth that turns customers into long-term, high-value ones, creating financial inclusion for Africa’s traditionally excluded. We’ve already helped over 10 million customers access over $2 billion in credit 🌍

The Opportunity

🏗️ Real ownership from day one. You'll be the one accountable for delivery in Repeat Phones, not shadowing or supporting someone else's plan.

🎒 Two growth motions, one year. You'll take on Digital Lending mid-way through, working directly with one of our strongest performers to understand cash loans end to end, then carry that pod solo for a defined stretch. Few people get this breadth this early.

🧭 A defined path, not indefinite floating. You'll build real expertise in our two conversion pods first, then move into Lifecycle in the second half of next year, reporting to the Lifecycle CRM Lead once you're there. The destination is set. What you bring to it is up to you. 🌍 Work inside a proven CLV engine. M-KOPA has helped more than 10 million customers access over $2 billion in credit. You'll be executing inside systems that already work, not guessing at what might.

What You'll Do

Phase 1: Repeat Phones. Take ownership of reactivation and upgrade campaigns in CleverTap, working closely with the Growth Lead there to understand what's driving the pod's numbers and where the next opportunity is. You'll be trusted to make real calls here, not just execute a checklist.

Phase 2: Cross into Digital Lending. Work directly with the Digital Lending lead, one of our top performers, to understand cash loan growth end to end before taking it on yourself.

Phase 3: Own Digital Lending. Carry primary responsibility for Digital Lending for a defined period, with the Repeat Phones lead available if you need a second opinion.

Phase 4: Move into Lifecycle. In the second half of next year, join the Lifecycle pod full-time, reporting to the Lifecycle CRM Lead. You'll bring a year of hands-on conversion experience into a pod that's still being built, real currency for shaping what Lifecycle does next. Throughout all phases, you will:

  • Build and run multi-channel campaigns (SMS, WhatsApp, push, in-app) in CleverTap against pod goals

  • Track funnel performance and flag drop-off points to the pod lead you're supporting

  • Run structured experiments (creative, audience, incentive, or timing) with clear hypotheses

  • Turn what works into documented playbooks the next person can pick up

  • Keep data quality and campaign tracking clean enough that leadership can trust the numbers

Key Metrics You'll Influence

Repeat Phones: Reactivation rate, upgrade conversion %, unit economics per sale

Digital Lending: Approval → disbursement rate, digital loan volume, approval quality

Campaign ROI and payback period across both

Your Environment

💼 Tech Stack: CleverTap (primary), Looker Channels: WhatsApp, SMS, push, in-app messaging

Markets: Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda, Ghana

What You Need

  • 5+ years in growth, performance, or lifecycle marketing, ideally in fintech, telco, or e-commerce, with real ownership over what a campaign or a pod achieved, not just involvement in it.

  • Judgment as much as skill. You can walk into a pod, understand what's working and why, and make calls on where to push, not just follow a brief.

  • Genuine appetite for pod leadership. This is a deliberate path toward owning a pod outright, and the breadth here is designed to get you there faster than a single-channel role would.

  • Hands-on fluency in CRM platforms like CleverTap, Braze, or similar, and comfortable reading a funnel or cohort without translation.

  • Energized, not unsettled, by ambiguity. You'll work across two pods and land in a third decision point by mid-year. If that sounds like an opportunity rather than a risk, you'll thrive here.

  • Strong enough presence to build trust quickly with senior leads across two different pods.

Location & Benefits

  • 🌍 Fully remote role within UTC -1 to UTC +3 time zones

  • 🤝 Work with diverse teams across UK, Europe, and Africa

  • 📚 Professional development programmes and coaching partnerships

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Family-friendly policies and flexible working arrangements

  • 💚 Well-being support and career growth opportunities

 

Our Mission 🌍

We create financial inclusion for the traditionally excluded through a fair, flexible, customer-centric financing model. We strive to drive greater inclusion of women, youth, and low-income communities.

 

Our Impact 💚

Our technology has created measurable change:

  • Connected 📱: 2.5 million first-time smartphone users connected

  • Prosperous 💰: 70% of customers use M-KOPA products for income generation, with 35,000+ livelihoods created for agents

  • Green 🌱: 2.1 million tonnes of CO₂ avoided through clean energy products, with over 127,700 circular economy products provided

 

Why M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com.

Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is seeking a 2LoD Compliance Strategist to provide dedicated independent second-line assurance across Ramp UK & Irish regulated businesses.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can turn regulatory expectations into a practical, evidence-led monitoring and assurance programme.

The role sits within Ramp's Europe Compliance function and supports the Head of Compliance & MLRO - Europe. You will not own first-line operational decisions or perform routine casework. Instead, you will independently test and challenge the design and operation of financial-crime, safeguarding, payments, outsourcing, governance, and regulatory-change controls. You will make sure that findings are understood, remediated by accountable owners, and independently validated before closure.

Ramp Payments Europe is developing across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions, payment rails, banking partners, product journeys, and shared Group services. The successful candidate will help give management and Boards a clear, reliable view of whether controls work in practice and where action is needed.

What You'll Do

  • Run a practical, risk-based compliance monitoring programme across Ramps European entities.

  • Test key controls and identify gaps, with a focus on whether they work in practice.

  • Support assurance over financial-crime, payments, safeguarding, and outsourced-service controls.

  • Track regulatory, Board, partner, audit, and internal commitments to ensure actions are completed on time.

  • Manage findings and remediation, helping accountable teams resolve issues and confirming actions are closed.

  • Produce clear reporting for management and Boards on key risks, control issues, incidents, and progress.

  • Provide independent compliance input and advisory on significant product, payments, outsourcing, and operational changes.

  • Deputise for the Head of Compliance & MLRO where required.

What You Need

  • Min. 4 year of experience in compliance, risk, audit, controls, or regulatory change within payments, fintech, banking, or another regulated environment.

  • Experience supporting compliance monitoring, control testing, issue management, remediation, or governance reporting.

  • Working knowledge of UK and/or EU financial-services regulation, with the ability to apply requirements pragmatically in a fast-moving environment.

  • Familiarity with financial-crime controls such as customer due diligence, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, or record keeping.

  • An interest in areas such as payments, safeguarding, outsourcing, operational resilience, or third-party oversight.

  • Strong judgement and communication skills, with the confidence to identify issues, explain risk clearly, and work constructively with stakeholders.

  • Comfortable working independently, managing priorities, and partnering with Product, Engineering, Operations, Legal, and Risk teams.

  • Curious about using AI responsibly to improve compliance analysis, monitoring, or documentation.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience in a UK payment institution, e-money institution, bank, card issuer, acquiring business, or payments fintech.

  • Experience supporting FCA-facing work, banking-partner due diligence requirements.

  • Experience with Consumer Duty, safeguarding, or formal outsourcing governance.

  • Professional compliance, audit, risk, or financial-crime qualification.

Account Executives are responsible for identifying, segmenting, engaging, and converting qualified Mid-Market and Enterprise prospects into paying customers according to an annual quota.


You will report to the Head of New Business, and will closely collaborate with all our teams (Marketing, Sales, Customer Care, Product and Finance) to drive maximum value and success with new Livestorm customers.


A successful Account Executive will be a skilled communicator and presenter who can find the best fit between client and product.

  • Work on the NEMEA (Nordics & UK) and US market (native speakers are preferred for this role / previous sales experience in these regions is a big plus).

  • Use of a variety of channels to identify new prospects and close new deals such as social media, internet, web-based tools & outbound calling

  • Manage effectively all CRM activity relating to your accounts (Salesforce) and all the tech stack of an AE at Livestorm (SalesNav, Salesloft, Modjo, Chili Piper, Notion & more)

  • Pro-actively work with other teams (Account Management, Growth & Marketing, Customer Success, etc.)

  • Provide clients’ feedback, especially on product, in order for Livestorm to adjust and prioritize its product roadmap.

  • Experienced: You have extensive experience (+3 years minimum) of successfully selling Software/SaaS license agreements into Enterprise / Large accounts in France and abroad across a variety of industries (expertise in the Finance & Healthcare industries is a plus)

  • Industry Knowledge: A good understanding of selling video communication platform would be ideal however, a background in selling SaaS and closing 6/7 figure deals is more important

  • Overachiever: You have consistently achieved and/or exceeded your sales goals across your geographic territory and have a track record in closing 6/7 figure contracts - You are results oriented

  • Outbound Mindset: You have a desire, even an obsession, to identify new prospects, contacts and decision makers to expand the number of new logos

    • Handle incidents and contingency: build the incident process around DNB, FIS and TARGET escalation routes, own Payment Ops’ role in DNB reporting, and define the ECONS II contingency approach.
    • Coordinate with others: work with the Eurosystem, DNB, SWIFT/NEXI, FIS and correspondent banks, and partner with Product and Engineering to specify how the platform should behave.

    What success looks like

    • Every direct-participation process has an owner, documented procedures, and passing UAT evidence.
    • The migration causes no impact on customers, and Customer Support has clear guidance.
    • After go-live, T2 runs as stable BAU with no remaining BNPP operational dependency.

    What we’re looking for

    • Hands-on experience with T2 / TARGET Services (RTGS, TIPS), including the GUI and U2A/A2A actions
    • Around 2-3+ years in payment operations at a bank, EMI or PSP, ideally with SEPA schemes (SCT, SCT Inst)
    • Familiarity with investigations, recalls, returns and SWIFT / ISO 20022 messaging
    • Experience writing SOPs and controls, or the ability to pick it up quickly
    • Comfort working with regulators, partners and technical teams
    • Enough ownership to make sign-off and escalation decisions with support from the team
    • Fluent English

    Nice to have

WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Build the machine that builds the machine. Join TechOps at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, we’re building the production system that will enable commercial fusion. The Production lines, tooling, and processes are being developed from the ground up; you'll create the ways of working, not inherit them.

  • Work at the frontier of manufacturing technology. Bring your creativity to evaluate, qualify, and deploy processes with no industry playbook, every component you build and every process you shape goes directly into the core of the stellarator magnet technology.

  • Do work that matters, and see it grow. The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world.

  • Make an impact you can point to. In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck.

YOUR IMPACT

You keep Alpha's cost and schedule baselines honest against each other. Without a credible risk register and change process, changes slip into the program outside any controlled path, the IMS and cost forecast quietly drift apart, and a gate review surprises leadership with numbers nobody signed off on. Your job is to prevent that by making risk and change management a live, trusted function from the earliest stage of delivery, rather than something bolted on once problems have compounded.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Establish and maintain the Alpha risk register across infrastructure, manufacturing and machine workstreams, facilitating structured risk identification, assessment and assignment of mitigation owners

  • Own the change control process end to end, from intake and schedule, cost and technical impact assessment through to approval routing and the change log, working closely with the Cost Controller and Programme Schedule Manager so all baselines reflect the same accepted changes

  • Prepare risk-adjusted inputs for release gate decisions, including quantified schedule and cost exposure and mitigation status

  • Run regular risk reviews with workstream owners and escalate emerging risks early, before they reach senior leadership as surprises

  • Build risk and change governance standards that scale as Alpha and Stellaris grow in parallel, with different partners and delivery models

  • Support the PMO's wider reporting cadence alongside the PMO Analyst/Coordinator


WHO YOU ARE

  • Experienced in risk and change management on major capital programs in energy, industrial, research infrastructure or similarly complex multi-discipline settings

  • Able to build a risk and change framework from scratch, not just administer an inherited one; you know what good governance looks like before it exists

  • Confident holding the line on change discipline with internal engineers and external partners who have their own priorities, combining analytical rigor with the communication skills to make it stick

  • Comfortable working with high autonomy while program structure is still being built

  • Fluent in English; German is a strong advantage given the contractor and regulatory landscape

  • Familiar with AI tools and digital ways of working, and quick to adapt in a lean, fast-paced environment

    INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Team

Our Infrastructure teams build the foundation that engineers at Wolt, Deliveroo, and DoorDash build on: the compute, cloud, and networking capabilities that enable Engineering teams to develop, deploy, and run services at global scale. The EU Compute team has a specific focus on provisioning, scaling, and the efficient operation of GPU infrastructure for AI and ML workloads. This is an emerging space with plenty of greenfield opportunities.

We're looking for a Staff Engineer to be a hands-on technical leader for this infrastructure work that crosses team and brand boundaries. You'll set direction for the platform, turn complex problems into deliverable plans, write and review production code, and help other engineers make sound decisions. It's an exciting time to join: we're building a global platform and the choices made now will shape how engineers across the company ship for years.

What you'll be doing

  • Use production signals and developer feedback to find platform friction, choose where to invest and measure whether changes actually help.
  • Assist with supporting the platform, with deep focus on GPU infrastructure, as well as broad focus on compute in general.
  • Gracefully sunset legacy infrastructure and tooling, and create strategies to reduce toil.
  • Mentor engineers through design reviews, implementation and incidents, raising the quality of infrastructure work across teams.

Our humble expectations

  • Strong software engineering skills: you use Go, Python or a similar language to build maintainable tools and automation.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code (we use Terraform) and with designing systems that other engineering teams depend on.
  • A track record of leading complex technical work across teams, including architectural decisions, delivery, and operational follow-through. You have the breadth to collaborate and design across team and domain boundaries, and the depth to have hands-on impact.
  • Strong judgment on trade-offs in distributed systems, networking, security, reliability, and cloud cost.
  • Clear communication, and the ability to bring people together around a practical technical direction.

Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.

We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.

This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.

We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.

This role will be based in London, UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.

What you'll do:

  • Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.
  • Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.
  • Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.
  • Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.
  • Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.
  • Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.
  • Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event.

Our expectations:

  • 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production.
  • 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly.
  • A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar).
  • Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability.
  • Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality.

Nice to have

  • Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud.
  • Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path.
  • Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go.
  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).
  • Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes.

What we value

  • A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them.
  • A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments.
  • Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together.
  • An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

About the Role:

Sitecore is seeking a dynamic and results-driven Field Marketing Manager to lead Net New demand generation for Digital Asset Management (DAM) across EMEA. This role will build market awareness, create qualified pipeline, and accelerate new customer acquisition through integrated field marketing aligned with regional go-to-market priorities.

You will develop and execute multi-channel programs that bring the DAM value proposition to target accounts and priority industries. Working closely with the DAM team, regional sales, business development, product marketing, and campaigns, you will turn audience and market insight into measurable pipeline. The ideal candidate is entrepreneurial, commercially minded, data-driven, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.

What You Will Do:

Strategy & Planning

  • Define and execute the Net New DAM demand generation strategy for EMEA, aligned with regional GTM, account priorities, and growth objectives

  • Build integrated field marketing plans that increase DAM awareness, engage buying groups, and convert priority accounts

Pipeline Generation

  • Deliver qualified DAM pipeline targets alongside regional sales leadership, business development, and the DAM team

  • Use account, intent, and market data to identify high-potential audiences, industries, and buying signals across EMEA

Field Marketing Programs

  • Design and deliver high-impact regional programs aligned with sales priorities, target account needs, and local market opportunities

  • Create connected journeys across events, digital activation, executive engagement, and sales follow-up to move accounts through the funnel

Campaign Execution

  • Localize and activate global DAM campaigns, adapting the value proposition, messaging, content, and tactics for EMEA audiences

  • Own the execution of field events, webinars, executive programs, and digital campaigns that support Net New DAM acquisition

Performance & Optimization

  • Track and report campaign engagement, sourced and influenced pipeline, conversion, and ROI using agreed dashboards and reporting frameworks

  • Continuously optimize audience, channel, content, and investment decisions based on performance data and stakeholder feedback

Collaboration & Enablement

  • Collaborate with the DAM team, Corporate Marketing, Product Marketing, Regional Sales, Business Development, and Sales Enablement to align plans and resources

  • Act as a trusted marketing advisor to sales teams, equipping them with DAM messaging, campaign plays, and timely follow-up guidance

What You Need to Succeed:

  • A minimum of 5 years of B2B marketing experience, ideally in SaaS, enterprise software, digital experience, content operations, or DAM

  • Proven success in field marketing with responsibility for Net New pipeline creation across multiple EMEA markets

  • Strong understanding of account-based marketing, buying groups, intent data, demand generation, and funnel acceleration

  • Experience designing and executing integrated field programs that engage target accounts and accelerate pipeline; DAM or content technology experience is advantageous

  • Excellent communication, program management, and stakeholder management skills across regional and global teams

  • Proficiency in marketing automation, CRM, account intelligence, and analytics platforms

  • Fluent in English; additional European languages and experience marketing across diverse EMEA markets are a plus

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Compliance team’s mission is to keep iwoca a safe and trusted lender for UK small businesses, and to make the compliant path the easy path for the teams we work with.

We make sure iwoca meets its regulatory obligations, particularly the financial crime, sanctions and data protection requirements that apply across our suite of products and services.

We are the second line of defence for the UK business. We advise the people building and running the business on what the rules require, set the policies and standards they work to, and test whether what happens in practice matches them. We work alongside the product teams so that each product meets its obligations and can grow.

Data protection is central to what we do. We hold the data privacy function for the UK business and own how iwoca handles personal data end to end: the lawful basis for how customer, applicant and third-party data is used; data subject access requests and other individual rights; personal data breaches; retention and deletion; records of processing; marketing and consent; the privacy review of new products and features; and the governance of automated decisioning and AI tooling.


How we work:

  • We enable rather than block. The answer is rarely just “no” — it’s what it would take to get to yes, and what the firm is accepting if it goes ahead anyway.

  • We go to the source. Positions are grounded in the actual rule, regulation or guidance, and we can show where they come from.

  • We’re proportionate. Controls match the risk in front of us. We don’t build process for its own sake.

  • We’re close to the business. We work directly with Tech, Data, Credit, Operations and Legal, and we want to be in the room early rather than at the end.

The role

As Data Privacy Analyst you will run iwoca’s day-to-day UK data protection work and help the business apply UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR in practice. Your primary focus will be the statutory core: data subject access requests, data protection impact assessments, legitimate interests assessments, personal data breaches and records of processing.

The role is not only to run that work but to improve it. A significant part of the job is identifying where our privacy operations could be automated, supported by AI or otherwise improved, assessing what each option would take and what it would mean for compliance, and specifying it well enough for our Tech and Data teams to deliver.

There is real room for the role to grow: as you build credibility, so does the scope, towards owning areas of the framework outright, leading on AI and automation governance, and taking a larger advisory remit across the business.

You will report to the Data Privacy Manager and work closely with the Head of Compliance who also acts as iwoca’s DPO, so you will have experienced support on the harder judgement calls. This is a hands-on role and the work is visible — much of it goes to senior stakeholders or to the regulator.

Impact and influence

  • Individual rights and data breaches. Own data subject access requests from intake to response — scoping the search, applying exemptions and meeting the statutory deadline — along with erasure, rectification and objection requests. Triage and investigate suspected personal data breaches, assess them against the 72-hour notification test, and keep the breach register accurate.

  • Privacy assessments and advice. Assist with DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments and other privacy reviews on new products, features, suppliers and data flows. Be an accessible first point of contact for teams across iwoca with a data protection question, and give them an answer they can act on, early enough to shape what they build.

  • Records, policies and reporting. Keep the record of processing activities accurate as the business changes, hold the retention and deletion schedules to account, review data processing agreements with suppliers, help maintain our data protection policies and standards, and produce the privacy reporting that goes to senior stakeholders.

  • AI and automated decisioning. Help assess AI tooling and automated decision-making across lending and operations: what personal data goes in, what lawful basis supports it, what the model does with it, and what rights customers have over the outcome. That includes the risks specific to these systems — decisions taken without meaningful human involvement, bias in outcomes, unreliable model output — and recommending how we address them.

  • Automation and improvement. Identify the manual steps in our privacy operations that should not be manual, assess the options, and set out the requirements and compliance implications clearly enough for Tech and Data to deliver them.

The requirements

Essential skills

  • Experience. Experience in data protection or privacy operations, or in a compliance, legal, risk or operational role where data protection was a real part of the job.

  • Data protection knowledge. A solid practical understanding of UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR, and of how the ICO expects firms to apply them. Familiarity with the changes made by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 is an advantage.

  • Privacy operations and assessments. Hands-on experience of statutory work: DSARs, DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments, breach handling, ROPA maintenance or data processing agreement review. You may not have done all of these — but we want to see that you have done some of them properly.

  • AI and automation. A real interest in, and working understanding of, how data protection law applies to AI and automated decision-making. Enough technical fluency to see where a manual process could be automated, set out what is needed, and hold your own in a conversation with engineers.

  • Stakeholder management: Comfortable dealing directly with product, engineering, marketing, credit and operations teams, and able to give a non-specialist a clear answer they can act on rather than a legal summary.

Bonus:

  • Sector experience. Financial services or fintech, ideally in lending or payments.

  • Credentials. A privacy or AI qualification such as CIPP/E, CIPM, or ICO-recognised practitioner certificates — or working towards one.

  • Practical tooling. Experience using Claude Code, LLMs or privacy management platforms.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

Business Development Manager

OUR MISSION

Carwow is Europe’s leading car-changing destination, transforming how people buy, sell, advertise, and lease cars through technology, media, and automotive expertise. From our beginnings as a reviews site, we’ve grown into one of the largest online marketplaces—facilitating nearly £3bn in car purchases and £1.8bn in sales listings last year alone. In 2024, we acquired Autovia (AutoExpress and Evo), doubling our audience and expanding our reach to 10 million YouTube subscribers, 1.2 million magazine sales, and 350m+ annual online readers. And we’re only just getting started.

YOUR MISSION

You’ll drive carwow’s buying platform adoption by winning and onboarding independent motor traders and franchise dealer groups through consultative selling and tailored demos. This is a phone-first role focused on high-volume outreach, with the flexibility to step into the field when it helps close key deals. You’ll be responsible for securing new partners, getting them bidding and buying quickly, and working with Account Management to maximise long-term growth.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Sign up new dealers and drive adoption - bidding and buying - on the Sell My Car platform.

  • Generate new business via cold outreach and inbound leads, primarily over the phone, with occasional field visits when required.

About Exeon

Exeon is a Swiss cyber security company based in Zurich. Since 2016, we have been protecting critical infrastructures, financial institutions and enterprises whose operations fully rely on IT through AI-powered analysis of network communication. This makes the most sophisticated cyberattacks visible – attacks conventional tools fail to detect. We combine Swiss excellence with a flexible, remote-first, and collaborative culture, supporting passionate, ambitious professionals devoted to solving cybersecurity challenges and driving continuous innovation.

What your impact will be like:

As a Systems Engineer in our Solutions team, you will help design the components and data flow of our core products: how data gets in, how deployments are configured and operated, and how everything scales across very different customer environments, many of them on-prem and air-gapped. 

You’ll split your time between building (ingestion pipelines, automation, tooling) and deploying and operating (working with customers to get Exeon running reliably in their environments), so your work shapes both scalability and customer success.

In particular, you will:

  • Build tooling and automation to simplify the deployment, configuration, and lifecycle management of Exeon.NDR, Exeon.UEBA, log collection and supporting components 

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable log ingestion pipelines for a wide range of network and application log sources and formats, including parsing, normalization, and validation 

  • Deploy and operate Exeon in customer environments (on-prem, private cloud, and hybrid), including sizing, performance tuning, and troubleshooting complex issues 

  • Work with customers to understand their data sources, infrastructure constraints, and security needs, and translate these into clear requirements for product and engineering teams 

  • Contribute to customer support, documentation, and runbooks alongside your Solutions colleagues

What you can expect from us:

Exeon offers an open company culture that values and encourages diversity, teamwork and a growth mindset. Our goal is to provide our employees with an exciting, supportive and motivating environment for personal growth and career development while ensuring that our team maintains a healthy work-life balance. We strive to achieve this by offering:

  • An exciting and impactful job in a fast-growing Swiss cyber tech company expanding across Europe with manifold opportunities to shape your professional profile.

  • Working in close collaboration with our interdisciplinary team and learning from our Security Experts, Data Scientists, and Business Professionals.

  • Taking over responsibilities quickly and help shape and promote a cutting-edge security software.

  • A high degree of trust, independence and flexibility, also in terms of working hours and place of work (remote or in the office).

  • A competitive salary and appealing benefits package.


What you bring along:

We are looking for a proactive, self-motivated and enthusiastic cyber security professional who is comfortable in a high-paced start-up environment and who shares our values. You should be confident with solving problems independently and communicating easily with both internal teams and directly with customers. You should also:

  • 3-5 years of experience in systems engineering, data engineering, platform/infrastructure engineering, or a similar role 

  • Working knowledge of network and application security and the telemetry relevant to detection 

  • UNIX/Linux experience, including networking, troubleshooting, and performance tuning in containerized deployments (Docker and/or Kubernetes) 

  • Strong programming skills in Python and Bash (or comparable languages), with a focus on automation and maintainable, production-quality code 

  • Hands-on experience designing and operating data ingestion pipelines (e.g. syslog, Logstash/Fluentd/Vector, Elastic stack, or similar), including handling heterogeneous formats and high volumes 

  • Comfortable with working in a largely remote team where clear communication is key to successful collaboration and impact. We are an English-speaking team but German fluency is appreciated when communicating to some customers 

  • Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience


Nice to have:

  • Solid understanding of network and application security fundamentals, common attack patterns, and the log and telemetry sources that matter for detection 

  • Experience with SIEM, SOAR, or detection platforms (e.g. Splunk, Sentinel, Elastic Security), or as a detection engineer or security analyst 

  • Familiarity with network telemetry such as NetFlow/IPFIX, Zeek, or Suricata, and frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK 

  • Prior customer-facing or professional services experience.

You create structure, challenge subject-matter experts, safeguard the strategy and quality, and keep stakeholders aligned throughout the process.   • Training and coaching colleagues who contribute to bids and helping to increase bid management maturity across the organisation;

You are a Bid Manager, not a Bid Writer

That distinction is important.

At Valcon, consultants, partners and subject-matter experts provide the content and contribute to the actual writing of bids. Some colleagues will be specifically trained to participate regularly in tender processes, while others may have limited experience with public tenders.

Your role is not to take over their writing. Instead, you ensure the team understands what is required, why it matters and when it needs to be delivered.

We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

How it works

 

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.

  • Regular use of an AI coding tool
  • Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
  • At least 10 hours a week, starting now
  • A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

 

Nice to have

 

  • Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
  • Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

 

Terms

 

  • US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
  • The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
  • Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

 

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

Job Description Summary

We are seeking an experienced Senior HR Compliance Manager to implement and sustain a robust HR compliance program across the EMENAT region (Europe, Middle East, North Africa and Turkey). Reporting into the wider HR leadership team, you will ensure adherence to applicable employment laws, regulations and internal policies, while enabling safe, high-quality and timely business operations through compliant and efficient HR practices.

In this role, you will lead risk assessments and audits, drive corrective actions through to completion, and partner with HR, Legal and business leaders to proactively manage compliance risk. As a trusted advisor and subject-matter expert, you will provide guidance that supports sound decision-making at all levels of the organisation. You will also manage and support employee investigations, including those that are complex in nature, ensuring they are handled fairly, consistently and in line with legal requirements.

Beyond regional responsibilities, you will contribute to global projects and initiatives, with the opportunity to lead cross-functional and cross-regional programmes. You will also be expected to support work outside your assigned region as business needs require.

Job Description

Core Responsibilities


Compliance Strategy and Governance

  • Drive a global-first HR compliance approach by standardizing policies, controls, and tools, and customizing locally to ensure full compliance with country-specific laws and practices.
  • Translate new regulations into actionable requirements, controls, and standard work
  • Chair or participate in regional compliance councils/working groups
  • Lead and support global initiatives and standards deployment; collaborate across regions to harmonize processes and share best practices
  • Support annual and ongoing HR compliance initiatives and projects as needed

Policy Management and Training

  • Draft, update, and harmonize HR policies, handbooks, and SOPs in partnership with Legal and Labor/Employee Relations
  • Develop and deliver training programs for HR, managers, and employees on critical topics (e.g., anti-discrimination, harassment prevention, pay, working time, leave, immigration and right to work, data privacy, and whistleblowing/speaking up)
  • Contribute to global policy alignment and change adoption across regions
  • Support HR Compliance programs related to pay transparency and equal pay requirements (including the EU Pay Transparency Directive and UK gender pay gap reporting) in partnership with Total Rewards and Legal

Investigations and Case Management

  • Manage and support regional employee investigations, including case assignment and investigation reviews
  • Conduct investigations that are complex in nature (e.g., multi-jurisdictional, senior leaders, potential regulatory exposure, or sensitive allegations)Partner with Legal, Employee Relations, and Security on investigatory strategy, privileged matters, and remediation
  • Ensure investigations comply with local requirements, including data protection (e.g., GDPR and UK GDPR), whistleblower protection and anti-retaliation rules, and any employee representative involvement
  • Drive investigation standards and reporting of metrics to stakeholders, including time to close, case volume, and trends
  • Support global cases as needed

Advisory and Regulatory Response

  • Provide expert guidance on complex employee relations, regulatory issues, and HR compliance requirements
  • Partner with Legal on labor inspectorate and other regulatory authority inquiries, employment tribunal or court claims, complaints, and remediation plans
  • Support due diligence and integration for M&A or site transitions, including cross-border regulatory considerations
  • Support Labor/Employee Relations and Legal relative to HR compliance aspects of works council, trade union, and employee representative information and consultation obligations, in partnership with Labor/Employee Relations and Legal

Regulatory Intelligence and Reporting

  • Monitor evolving laws and regulations across the region; maintain a regulatory calendar
  • Ensure timely filings, certifications, and statutory reports
  • Prepare executive updates, dashboards, and compliance metrics; contribute to global reporting where required

Global Projects and Cross-Regional Support

  • Lead or support global HR compliance projects, tool deployments, and change initiatives
  • Provide subject-matter support outside the assigned region as needed; coordinate with global and regional leaders to ensure consistent implementation
  • Share best practices and lessons learned across regions to improve efficiency and effectiveness
  • Serve as sub-risk focal for one or more Labor risk areas.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business or Law, or equivalent professional experience
  • Significant experience in HR compliance advisory and management across the EMENAT region (Europe, Middle East, North Africa, and Turkey), including employee relations, investigations case management, and policy management in a global or multi-jurisdictional environment
  • Demonstrated ability to lead compliance programs, interpret and operationalize regulations, manage complex investigations, advise on regulatory and employee relations matters, develop policies and training, support audits/reporting, and drive cross-regional HR compliance initiatives
  • Experience with HRIS, case management, and compliance monitoring tools; proficiency with data analysis and reporting
  • Experience in managing global HR Compliance initiatives
  • Deep knowledge of regional employment law and HR compliance frameworks, including data protection (GDPR/UK GDPR) as applied to employment; experience interpreting and operationalizing complex regulations
  • Fluency in written and spoken English

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bi-lingual English-Italian or English-Polish preferred
  • Advanced degree or compliance/HR certification (e.g., CCEP, CIPD, SHRM-SCP, SPHR) preferred
  • Experience with FLIGHT DECK or other LEAN /Six Sigma Process
  • Experience supporting global or regional HR compliance programs in a complex, matrixed, and multi-jurisdictional organization
  • Experience drafting and implementing HR policies, handbooks, SOPs, controls, and governance frameworks in partnership with Legal and Employee Relations
  • Proven ability to translate regulatory changes into practical operational requirements, training, and standard work
  • Experience developing and delivering compliance training for HR, managers, and employees
  • Experience using AI to streamline work and create solutions
  • Strong analytical and project leadership skills, including experience with compliance metrics, dashboards, reporting, and risk tracking
  • Experience partnering with cross-functional stakeholders such as Legal, Labor/Employee Relations, Security, HR leaders, and regional business teams
  • Experience supporting M&A, integrations, site transitions, or other organizational change initiatives involving HR compliance considerations
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, influence at multiple levels of the organization, and drive consistent global standards with appropriate local customization

Key Competencies

  • Regulatory expertise
  • Strong stakeholder management, influencing, and change leadership across matrixed and cross-border organizations
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and presentation skills; ability to translate regulatory concepts into practical guidance
  • Policy development and training
  • Analytical problem-solving
  • Program management and execution
  • Cross-cultural communication and collaboration
  • Continuous improvement mindset

Flexible Working
We supports and encourages flexible working arrangements, where possible, and recognises the benefits to employees of having a positive work-life balance.


Security Clearance
Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance is required and must be maintained for this role. Please note that in the event that BPSS clearance cannot be obtained, you may not be eligible for the role and/or any offer of employment may be withdrawn on grounds of national security. Please see the link below for further details regarding the requirements for BPSS clearance: BPSS

Right to Work
Applications from job seekers who require sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. However, under the applicable UK immigration rules as may be in place from time to time, it may be that candidates who do not currently have the right to work in the UK may not be appointed to a post if a suitably qualified, experienced and skilled candidate who does not require sponsorship is available to take up the post. Job Description

CLEAResult is seeking an experienced and highly analytical Finance Manager to lead financial planning, reporting, forecasting, and controllership activities across the organization. This role will serve as a key business partner to operational and regional leaders, providing actionable financial insights that support strategic decision-making and operational excellence.


The Finance Manager will own critical financial processes including budgeting, forecasting, monthly reporting, variance analysis, and financial performance reviews. Additionally, this leader will oversee a small team, develop finance talent, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data used by executive leadership.


Key Responsibilities


Financial Reporting & Analysis

  • Prepare and distribute monthly consolidated financial performance reports, summarizing results by region and business line.
  • Develop monthly management reporting packages that clearly communicate business performance, key trends, and variances to budget, forecast, and prior year results.
  • Analyze revenue, operating expenses, and capital expenditures, identifying financial risks, opportunities, and recommended corrective actions.
  • Perform detailed variance analysis and reconciliations against forecasts and annual operating plans.

Forecasting, Budgeting & Planning

  • Lead the consolidated forecasting and annual budgeting processes across multiple regions and business lines.
  • Partner with operational and business leaders to develop accurate financial projections and support strategic decision-making.
  • Monitor financial performance throughout the year and provide recommendations to achieve financial objectives.
  • Ensure consistency and accuracy of financial submissions from regional and business line finance teams.

Controllership & Close Process

  • Manage the monthly close process, including preparation and review of accruals, reclassification entries, and other adjustments necessary to ensure financial accuracy.
  • Maintain ownership of below-the-line bookings and associated forecasts, ensuring completeness and compliance with financial reporting requirements.
  • Prepare Income Statement (IS) and Balance Sheet (BS) reporting used in the calculation and reporting of Credit EBITDA.
  • Partner with accounting and finance teams to ensure strong financial controls and reporting integrity.

Business Development & Contract Reporting

  • Produce and maintain new business reporting, including bookings, pipeline conversion metrics, and related performance indicators.
  • Manage and report on the contract database, including tracking won contract values and business growth metrics.
  • Provide analysis of sales performance and business development trends to support growth initiatives.

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Lead, coach, and develop finance professionals, fostering a high-performance and collaborative team environment.
  • Build strong partnerships with operational, commercial, and executive leadership teams to support strategic and financial objectives.
  • Drive continuous improvement in financial processes, reporting methodologies, and planning tools.

Qualifications


Required Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • 7-10 years of progressive finance, FP&A, accounting, or corporate finance experience.
  • 1-2 years of experience leading and developing teams.
  • Demonstrated experience owning the budget, forecast, and financial reporting cycle for a business unit, function, or organization.
  • Strong experience preparing executive-level financial reporting and performance analysis.
  • Proven ability to partner effectively with operational leaders and influence business decisions through data-driven insights.
  • Experience managing monthly close processes and financial reporting requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • MBA, CPA, CMA, or other relevant financial certification.
  • Experience in professional services, energy, sustainability, consulting, or project-based organizations.
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel, financial modeling, and enterprise financial systems.
  • Experience working with large datasets and business intelligence/reporting tools.

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

As a Core AE, you will be helping our largest and most strategic enterprise sized customers consolidate outdated technologies, digitize workflows, and unlock game-changing data insights that will transform their businesses. We are helping the companies that literally keep our lights on, put food on our tables, and build our communities to become safer, more efficient, and more sustainable. Typical sales will be $100k to $500k, and typically involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US and requires working in EST and CST timezone.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
  • You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
  • You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop Executive-Level relationships within strategic, named accounts
  • Own customer engagements end-to-end, from prospecting and qualification to close
  • Demonstrate excellent solution-based sales process in complex sales campaigns
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
  • Proven track record of consistent quota over-achievement in complex accounts and $100k+ ARR transactions
  • Experience handling and owning enterprise deal sizes and C-Level relationships
  • Willing and comfortable with strategic outbound prospecting
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast paced environment
  • Willing and comfortable traveling to meet customers on a monthly basis

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience working with line of business stakeholders (Operations, Finance, IT)
  • Awards for top achievement (President’s club, Winner’s circle, Top 10%)
  • Passion for the world of operations!

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Belonging at Samsara

Accommodations
